---
title: "User manual"
---

onthesignal is an interactive console, also available in the browser as a web interface: you
load records (miniSEED or text files, or a SeedLink acquisition), run analyses with `/`
commands or Python expressions, look at tables and figures, and generate reports.

- [Installation](installation.qmd) and [quick start](quickstart.qmd)
- [Web interface](web.qmd): everything in the browser (`onthesignal web`), with a Python
  terminal, an editor and the AI chat
- [Conventions](conventions.qmd): units, sensitivity, dB, dBFS, times
- [Files](files.qmd): miniSEED, text files, export
- [Test signals](test-signals.qmd): sine and noise from an ideal N-bit digitizer
- [Command reference](commands.qmd): every `/` command and Python function
- [Measurement procedures](measurement.qmd): digitizer self-noise, sine tests, NLNM comparison
- [Acquisition and real time](acquisition.qmd)
- [Scripts and batches](scripts.qmd)
- [Reports](reports.qmd)
- [AI assistant](ai.qmd)
- [Configuration](configuration.qmd)
- [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd)

The computations are described in the [Algorithms](../algorithms/index.qmd) part.
